title: UnityGameTranslator server-sent events
description: What travels on the four streams the relay (website/sse-server/server.js) serves, and how the site feeds them. The site never writes a stream itself: it PUBLISHES a message on a Redis channel (App\Services\SsePublisher) and, for answers a client may miss, STORES the same message under a key; the relay subscribes, replays what was stored, and writes the wire. A client reads the wire with a plain SSE parser (the mod's Engine/SseStream) and hands each event's `data` to a reader (Engine/ApiReaders). Held by: check-spec.py (the cases against these schemas), tests/Unit/SsePublisherContractTest.php (the site publishes exactly these messages), Core.Checks/SseEventsChecks (the mod parses these frames and derives these values).
x-relay-note: The relay has no test runner of its own: it is one file without exports, and cutting it up is a decision for another day. Its wire format is therefore described here from a reading of server.js (2026-09-11) and proved from the OTHER end — the frames the mod's parser is held to are written in exactly that format.

base.url: https://unitygametranslator.asymptomatikgames.com:3000 (production) — compiled into the mod as SseBaseUrl; config.json's sse_base_url overrides it. The relay listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 behind the site's reverse proxy.
base.health: GET /health (or /) → {status: "ok", uptime_s, revalidate_interval_s, and — with the configured X-Health-Token — connections, max_connections, peak_connections, refused_at_capacity, refused_per_ip, refused_attempts, per_ip_limit, per_ip_attempts_per_minute}. Not a stream.

wire.preamble: `retry: 3000\n\n` as the first bytes of every stream: the reconnection delay the client starts from (SseStream.RetryDelayMs).
wire.event:
`id: <n>
event: <name>
data: <one-line JSON>

` — `n` counts from 1 per CONNECTION (it restarts on every reconnect; nothing is replayed by id, see `replay`). `data` is one line: the payload is serialised without newlines.
wire.heartbeat: `: heartbeat\n\n` every 15 s (HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS) on every stream; a comment line the parser drops. A client that hears nothing for 60 s treats the stream as gone (SseStream.HeartbeatTimeoutMs) and reconnects.
wire.last_event_id: The client sends `Last-Event-ID` on a reconnect (SseClient) and the relay IGNORES it: what a client may have missed is replayed from the stored message, not by id. The header is harmless and kept for a relay that might one day use it.

client.authorization: `Authorization: Bearer ugt_…` on the sync stream ONLY. The device, merge and edit streams are authorised by the code, token or key in their path.
client.reconnect: On end of stream, a dropped connection or a heartbeat timeout: wait the retry delay (3 s, doubled up to 30 s, reset on a successful connection), reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`. A stream opened for ONE event (device flow) stops once it has it (SseClient.StopAfterFirstEvent) — the relay closing it then is the ordinary end, not a loss.
client.definitive: 401, 403 and 404 at the door are final: the client stops and reports the body. 429, 5xx and network failures are retried with the backoff.
client.revoked: A sync stream whose access is cut receives `error {code: "revoked"}` and is closed by the relay: the client signs out, exactly as on an HTTP 401. Any other `error` is a stream that ended, which the connection loop handles.

expected.description: A device code or a merge token must have been ANNOUNCED by the site before a stream may open on it: SsePublisher::expected writes `sse:<kind>:<code>:pending` for the code's lifetime, and the marker `sse:expected` (never expiring) says this site announces. The relay demands the announcement only while the marker exists — so the two deploy in any order — and also accepts a code whose `:result` is already stored.

device.auth: the device code in the path (secret to the client)

stored.delivery: once — the relay deletes the key once the frame has left the process, so a client holding the code cannot be handed the token twice; the TTL bounds the wait for a client whose stream was not yet open

device.lifetime: ONE event, then the relay closes the stream.

authorized.description: The person typed the code on /link and confirmed. The token is delivered here and nowhere else; the client stores it and signs in.

expired.description: The code's fifteen minutes ran out — from the relay's own timer (`{error: "Timeout"}`) or from the site (`{error: "Device code expired"}`).

error.description: The relay could not subscribe (`{error: "Internal error"}`).

sync.auth: `Authorization: Bearer` — checked at the door against GET /me (401 on refusal, 502 when the site does not answer), and again every 5 minutes on the open stream (REVALIDATE_INTERVAL_MS): a refusal then closes it with `error {code: revoked}`.

query.hash: optional, ≤256: the `file_hash` held, so `state.has_update` can be answered.
query.lineage: `0` asks about the caller's own row only — what every stream the mod opens sends (GetSyncSseUrl). Anything else leaves the payload whole, which a mod older than the parameter expects.

channels: sse:translation:{id} — the caller's own row, or the Main's when the caller holds none
sync.lifetime: Long-lived: the client reconnects on end of stream (the hour, a drop) and receives a fresh `state` first.

state.description: First frame of every connection, and again whenever ANYBODY publishes into the lineage (`uuid_changed` on the site's side): the body of GET /sync/state, re-read with the caller's scope. Rule 1 of the API applies with a twist a client must implement: with `lineage=0` the lineage fields are ABSENT, and the client KEEPS what a fuller answer established (ApiReaders.ReadSyncState) — absent means unknown, never none.

translation_updated.description: The row the stream watches moved: an upload, a merge, a vote. Carries the new fingerprint so the client compares it with its own without a round trip.

error.description: `{error: "Access revoked", code: "revoked"}` when the access was cut while the stream was open — then the relay closes it; `{error: "Internal error"}` when the relay could not subscribe.

uuid_changed.description: Published by the site on `sse:uuid:{uuid}` whenever anybody publishes into the lineage. Never written to a client: the relay re-reads GET /sync/state with the caller's scope and emits a `state`.

merge.auth: the token in the path (POST /merge-preview/init answered it)
merge.lifetime: ONE event, then the relay closes the stream.

merge_completed.description: The page arbitrated. `destination: local` (with `translation_id` and `line_count`, no `file_hash`): the result is collected from GET /merge-preview/{token}/result; otherwise (`translation_id`, `file_hash`, `line_count`) it IS the published translation, downloaded as any other.

merge_preview_ended.description: The comparison is over without a result: the page was closed, or the mod let go (DELETE /merge-preview/{token}). Overwrites any stored result. `data: []`.

edit.auth: the 64-character mod key in the path (POST /edit-session/init answered it; never shown to a browser)

stored.delivery: REPLAYED on every (re)connection, after the subscription is open: the latest `edit_saved` — or `edit_session_ended`, which overwrites it and closes the stream at once. The client dedupes a replayed save on `content_hash`.

edit.presence: This connection IS the holder being there: the relay writes `sse:edit:{mod_key}:game` with a token, renews it on every heartbeat (TTL max(45 s, 3 heartbeats)), and releases it on close only if the token is still its own — a reconnecting client opens its new stream before the old one finishes closing. A holder that polls instead of streaming claims presence itself (`GET /edit-session/{key}/state?following=1`).
edit.lifetime: Long-lived: MANY events over one connection; the client reconnects on end of stream (the hour, a drop) until `edit_session_ended`.

edit_saved.description: The browser saved: fetch GET /edit-session/{key}/content and merge it with the live file. Replayed on reconnection (stored); `content_hash` is the dedupe key.

edit_session_ended.description: The page ended the session. Stored in place of the last save, so a replay cannot send the client to a file that is gone. `data: []`.

browser_left.description: The page's leave beacon fired (close, refresh, navigation): the client starts its grace timer (EditSessions.BrowserGraceSeconds). Not stored — presence also rides the answers to the client's own pushes. `data: []`.

browser_joined.description: The page (re)signalled presence after having been marked away: the grace timer is cancelled. `data: []`.

edit_retranslate.description: The page asks the holder to translate ONE line again with the holder's own backend; the answer goes back by POST /edit-session/{key}/retranslation as a proposal. Not stored (a replay would ghost-retranslate): the page re-emits every ~30 s with the SAME `id` while pending, and the client dedupes on it.

access_token.description: The bearer token: stored as config.json's api_token, sent on every authenticated call.

code.description: Named only when a client must ACT on it rather than show it.

content_updated_at.description: Sent by the API upload path; the site's merge paths do not send it.

destination.description: Present only when the result stays local.

file_hash.description: Present only when the result was published.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the session file after the save — the dedupe key.

key.description: The source line to translate again.

id.description: The page's request id, stable across its retries.
